cards.source: REF 4.2.2 (scribd 814006944) recovers Jumla verbatim. SHIPS ON ITS FIRST SENTENCE ALONE - 'This is an extra Ideology Card' - put to you at your next turn. DROPPED for NAMED gaps: 'of your choice' is G17; the price an opponent pays is G15's price field; re-filing under another Ideologue is G23. Same archetype as HOLO SAPIENS per REF 4.2.2: one template, two skins, one reduction. Argument in KNOWN-GAPS.md G20.
cards.name: Jumla
cards.text: This is an extra Ideology Card. You will be put it at the start of your next turn, face down, and you will not be told which one.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2 rule 5. SUBSTITUTE for CULT-IVATING OBEDIENCE (REF 4.2.2), RULED OUT in KNOWN-GAPS.md 8.3 - and its gap label is wrong twice over: the card itself is the object that is captured, so it is G11 and NOT G20, because no move-card reaches it. A capture also needs the protected majority to SURVIVE it, so it is a persisted per-zone protection plus a transfer, and the engine has no per-zone flag. Same JOB, the half that survives: protection the table can feel. The 'somebody may buy it' half is DROPPED and named.
cards.name: The Quiet Room
cards.text: For the rest of this round, no opponent may use an unlocked Ideologue Power.

cards.source: original; register per REF 8.2 rule 5. SUBSTITUTE for CHAI-PAANI, which KNOWN-GAPS.md section 7 rules is NOT A GAP AT ALL: only a re-application clause was recovered ('A second Chai-Paani card can be applied on the same player. The first one will get deactivated'), the base effect was never recovered, and inventing one is forbidden. Same JOB - one protection at a time, the newest replacing the oldest - expressed as a rule with a deadline rather than as persistent state.
cards.name: Second Helping
cards.text: Until the end of your turn, no opponent receives any resources for answering an Ideology Card - neither the answer's resources nor their passive bonus. Their answer still succeeds.
